profile.reading:
Csquare IAD1-A sits at 45901 Nokes Boulevard, Sterling, Virginia 20166, one of three buildings (IAD1-A, IAD1-B, IAD1-C) on Csquare's IAD1 campus in Loudoun County's Northern Virginia data center corridor. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists IAD1-A individually at 48,031 square feet sellable, 46.7 percent leased as of March 31, 2026; Csquare's public spec sheet gives only a combined campus total across all three IAD1 buildings, 141,621 square feet of raised floor, 143.2 megawatts of utility power, 19.8 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 37.5 megawatts of generator capacity, with chilled-water cooling and SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, and ENERGY STAR certifications applicable campus-wide rather than broken out per building. The SEC filing's summed IAD1-A/B/C square footage (roughly 143,353 square feet) runs about 1.2 percent above the website's combined campus figure, a minor discrepancy likely reflecting differing sellable-versus-raised-floor measurement conventions rather than a data error. All three IAD1 buildings are leased rather than Csquare-owned, per the SEC filing. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date for IAD1-A; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD1 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, alongside dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators within a few miles. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026, and the same filing notes the company's legal predecessor entity, BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, was formed in May 2018 as a Brookfield Infrastructure Fund III vehicle, well before the 2024 Cyxtera and Evoque combination that produced the assets tracked in this dataset.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

profile.research_note: Sqft is the SEC S-1 per-building figure for IAD1-A specifically (48,031 sqft sellable, 46.7% leased). Power figures (143.2MW utility, 19.8MW UPS, 37.5MW generator) are published only campus-wide across all three IAD1 buildings (A/B/C), not broken out per building, so no capacity figure was attributed to this specific row.

reading.body:
Centersquare IAD1-A is one of three clustered facilities in Sterling, Virginia sharing a single published specification. The operator's market page reports 143.2 MW of utility power and 141,621 square feet of raised floor for the combined Sterling IAD1 campus, though no breakdown among the three sites is published. Without knowing how this capacity is distributed across IAD1-A, IAD1-B, and IAD1-C, the individual contribution of this facility to grid demand cannot be determined from available data.

Virginia has 23 data center facilities with published power figures totaling 1375.4 MW across 326 mapped sites statewide. If the full 143.2 MW Sterling IAD1 figure were assigned to this row, it would rank 24th in the state, but the actual allocation is unpublished. The state context alone does not indicate whether this campus supports the published certifications or market segments that would signal AI workload concentration.

No IT load density, cooling architecture, power delivery standard, network provider, or grid interconnection details are published for this facility. Assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, 143.2 MW could serve approximately 3,580 racks, but this calculation relies on neither operator data nor confirmation that AI workloads occupy this site. Without published specifications beyond location and the combined power figure, this campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI scaling constraints.
